chunks: Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
Ali عليه السلام used to milk the sacrificial camel and allow riding upon it, without causing harm.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: A kunyah referring here to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام.
key_terms.الْبَدَنَةَ: The sacrificial camel offered in hajj rites.
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ: Imam Ali عليه السلام, whose practice is being reported.
key_terms.مَنْصُورُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ: A narrator transmitting this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام.
key_terms.يَحْلُبُ: He milked; taking milk from the sacrificial camel.
key_terms.يَحْمِلُ عَلَيْهَا: He would have riding or carrying upon it.

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to milk or ride a sacrificial camel in Islam if it is not harmed?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates the permissibility of benefiting from a sacrificial camel by milking it and riding it. The condition stated is that no harm be caused to the animal, showing a legal and ethical limit in the use of sacrificial animals.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3087 - Mansur ibn Hazim narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
"Imam Ali (as) used to milk the sacrificial camel and allow others to ride it, provided it was not harmed."
